report:
Reviewed the complete item_origin claim and all three ordinary implementation entries (parse/util.rs::item_start, parse/items.rs::parse_associated_items, parse/attrs.rs::parse_attr_nodes), the ordinary associated-item regression, and the explicit TODO test. Dependencies used for dispatch, fixture setup, representation, and policy were captured with review read after restarting on the final implementation and association set.

Requirements: (1) each represented item's origin is the earliest first attribute or item-node start; (2) resulting attribute offsets are nonnegative; (3) entering an associated definition resets offsets to that definition's origin rather than its trait/impl origin. util::item_start returns the first pending attribute start, or the node start when there are no attributes. The recorded parse_item_list traverses children in source order and accumulates preceding attributes, so the first pending attribute is earlier than the following item node; an explicit min is not needed for these parser inputs. The source-root constructors in items.rs consistently use this origin for their absolute span and CST parsing. Error items also use item_start, while dangling attributes form an error span beginning at the first attribute.

For nested definitions, both parse_trait and parse_impl enter parse_associated_items with the owner's origin. That function now selects child_start from the child's pending attributes before clearing them; placement.start is child_start minus the owner origin and placement.end remains the child end minus the owner origin. Function/signature, associated type/type item, and constant branches pass this new child origin and retained attributes into their private CST helpers. Each helper sets the full item's own span start to zero and end to node.end minus child_start, and passes child_start into its signature/body parsing. Thus the owner-relative placement and child-relative content have distinct bases. parse_attr_nodes retains represented attributes (evaluated true cfg attributes are intentionally omitted), and parse_one_attr subtracts that same origin from each attribute start/end. Empty attribute lists remain empty. False cfg items are skipped before CST construction, comments do not consume pending associated attributes, and unsupported associated bodies retain the existing error-item path.

The initial implementation failed an anchor-associated behavioral regression. Command cargo test -p sage-ir --test item_origin, test associated_item_origin_includes_first_attribute, used trait Example { #[allow(dead_code)] fn member(); }; expected the composed method origin at byte 16 (attribute), but observed byte 36 (fn). This was an assertion failure, not a compilation failure. The coordinated fix retains pending attributes until the supported child is parsed, chooses the attribute-inclusive child origin, and stores the attributes in the three child CST kinds. The original failure is covered by the stronger final test.

The complete ordinary test body visibly loops over trait and impl owners, function/type/constant members, and absent versus two attributes (12 scenarios). A nonzero file prefix and an attributed owner distinguish absolute source, owner, and member bases. It asserts the owner's attribute-inclusive absolute start, exactly one member, composed placement start/end against source-derived byte positions, zero child CST start and the full attributed member length, empty attributes for plain members, and exact start/end offsets for both retained attributes. Choosing the enclosing origin, dropping an attribute, starting at the item keyword, truncating the item's range, or retaining owner-relative child ranges breaks these assertions. parse_fixture is captured: it creates a root source/scope and calls the real parser; meaningful assertions are not hidden in the helper.

The second test, sage_meta::todo::types_spans_item_origin, has no assertions and remains honestly deferred. Its requested focused attribute/nested coordinates now have partial substantive coverage from the ordinary regression, but the explicit empty and error-node fixtures remain absent. Completing those scenarios requires parser fixtures that expose empty/malformed node byte coordinates and assert their origins; the empty TODO function does not prove those edge cases. The test set therefore combines verified supported-item cases with a preserved explicit edge-case test deferral, not a claim of exhaustive test completion. There are no N/A or implementation TODO entries.

Execution: cargo fmt --all completed. The final cargo test -p sage-ir --test item_origin passed (one test covering 12 scenarios). cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_tests configuration_selects_items_before_checking and cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_tests modules_and_associated_bodies each passed. Existing compiler warnings were unrelated. Workspace build, full suites, and independent quality/sanity checks are coordinated by root and are not claimed as executed by this reviewer. Source inspection plus the reproduced/fixed regression accounts for the claim; the explicit edge-case test TODO remains visible. No further edits are requested.
